p: from Edom: This prophecy is against the Idumeans and enemies who persecuted the Church, on whom God will take vengeance, and is here set forth all bloody after he has destroyed them in Bozrah, the chief city of the Idumeans: for these were their greatest enemies,and under the title of circumcision and the kindred of Abraham.
I that speak in righteousness: God answers them that asked this question, "Who is this?" etc. and says "You see now performed in deed the vengeance which my prophets threatened."
Why art thou red in thy: Another question, to which the Lord answers.
year of my redeemed is come: Showing that when God punishes his enemies, it is for the profit and deliverance of his Church.

arm brought salvation to me: God shows that he has no need of man's help for the deliverance of his, and though men refuse to do their duty through negligence and ingratitude, yet he himself will deliver his Church, and punish the enemies, Isa 59:16.
drunk in my fury: I will so astonish them and make them so giddy that they will not know which way to go.
mention the lovingkindnesses of the LORD: The prophet speaks this to move the people to remember God's benefits in times past, that they may be confirmed in their troubles.
people: For I chose them to be mine, that they should be holy, and not deceive my expectation.
afflicted: He bore their afflictions and griefs as though they had been his own.
of his presence saved them: Which was a witness of God's presence, and this may be referred to Christ, to whom belongs the office of salvation.
remembered the days of old: That is, the people of Israel being afflicted, called to mind God's benefits, which he had bestowed on their fathers in times past.
shepherd of his flock: Meaning, Moses.
him: That is, in Moses that he might well govern the people: some refer this giving of the spirit to the people.
horse in the wilderness: Peaceably and gentle, as a horse is led to his pasture.
Look down from heaven: Having declared God's benefits showed to their forefathers, he turned himself to God by prayer, desiring him to continue the same graces toward them.
zeal and thy strength: Your great affection, which you bore for us.
restrained: Meaning, from the whole body of the Church.
Abraham be ignorant of us: Though Abraham would refuse us to be his children, yet you will not refuse to be our father.

thou made us to err from: By taking away the Holy Spirit from us, by whom we were governed, and so for our ingratitude delivered us up to our own concupiscence, and punished sin by sin according to your just judgment.
servants' sake: Meaning, for the covenant's sake made to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob his servants.

while: That is, in respect to the promise, which is perpetual: even though they had now possessed the land of Canaan for 1400 years: and thus they lament, to move God rather to remember his covenant, than to punish their sins.
